critical_code_review_comments: audit_trail_routes.py sign_entry() uses insertion-time keys id/action/user_id/created_at only. A malicious editor with DB access could still tamper fields like details, ip_address, status, risk_level without breaking the HMAC. Recommend hashing the entire canonicalized entry (excluding sig) — otherwise 'tamper-proof' claim is overstated.

archive endpoint uses db.audit_logs.delete_one({'_id': d['_id']}) — an ObjectId delete. Since audit_logs also contains legacy AuditLogger docs, archive would silently remove them too. Consider filtering only signed entries or requiring dual-role approval.

REPORT_PRESETS['device'] filter uses user_agent existence but most legacy logs store user_agent inside details/client — the preset may miss device data; recommend widening to {'$or':[{'user_agent':...},{'client.user_agent':...},{'details.user_agent':...}]}.
